MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  January 12, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:05 p.m., on Monday, January 12, 2026, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  LEE, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Management Analyst Alvarez, Lieutenant Lee, Building Division
Manager Turango, Building Official Jefferson

FLAG SALUTE:  Led by Mayor Maloney

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M26-4

Mayor MALONEY stated that City staff would be in contact to try and address concerns.

PUBLIC HEARING

3.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE ALHAMBRA
  MUNICIPAL CODE BY MODIFYING TITLE 20 THEREOF ADOPTING BY REFERENCE,
  THE 2025 CALIFORNIA BUILDING, RESIDENTIAL, ELECTRICAL, MECHANICAL,
  PLUMBING, ENERGY, HISTORICAL BUILDING, EXISTING BUILDING, AND GREEN
  BUILDING STANDARDS CODES, WITH CERTAIN AMENDMENTS, ADDITIONS, AND
  DELETIONS THERETO – F2M25-60, N2M25-181, O2M25-4853

  Building Division Manager TARANGO delivered a staff report. Staff requested that the City
  Council conduct a public hearing and, after receiving public testimony, consider second
  reading and adoption of an ordinance adopting by reference the 2025 California Building,
  Residential, Electrical, Mechanical, Plumbing, Energy, Historical Building, Existing Building,
  and Green Building Standards Codes, with certain amendments, additions, and deletions
  thereto. Every three years, the California Building Standards Commission (CBSC) publishes
  an updated edition of Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations, known collectively as the
  “California Building Standards Code”. The 2025 edition of Title 24 was published on July 1,
  2025, and became effective January 1, 2026, statewide. California Codes can be viewed at:
  https://www.dgs.ca.gov/BSC/Codes. State law (California Health and Safety Code § 18938.5)
  requires all cities to enforce these updated codes. Cities may also adopt local amendments,
  where justified by local climatic, geological, or topographical conditions, and such findings
  2
1-12-26
   must be filed with the California Building Standards Commission. For this code adoption cycle,
  City of Alhambra adopted the 2025 California Building Standards Code directly, without
  incorporating the Los Angeles County amendments. Recent state legislation, Assembly Bill
  (AB) 130 (2025), placed a moratorium on the adoption of new residential building code
  modifications that exceed State minimum standards. The proposed ordinance fully complied
  with AB 130. No new local amendments to the Building Code or Residential Code were
  introduced as part of this adoption. The proposed ordinance also reorganized Title 20 of the
  Alhambra Municipal Code to improve clarity and efficiency. The proposed ordinance was
  introduced for first reading at the December 8, 2025 City Council meeting.

  Opened & Closed the Public Hearing: Mayor MALONEY opened the public hearing and as
  there was no one present who wished to speak, closed the same.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council conducted a public hearing and, after receiving public
  testimony, declared introduced for its second reading and adopt the following ordinance
  entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M25-4853: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City Council
  amending the Alhambra Municipal Code by modifying Title 20 thereof adopting
  by reference, the 2025 California Building, Residential, Electrical, Mechanical,
  Plumbing, Energy, Historical Building, Existing Building, and Green Building
  Standards Codes, with certain amendments, additions, and deletions thereto

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

PRESENTATIONS

4.  ORDINANCE PROHIBITING THE SALE AND DISTRIBUTION OF NITROUS OXIDE AND
  DETERMINATION THAT THE ORDINANCE IS EXEMPT FROM CEQA – F2M25-7, O2M26-
  4856

  Deputy City Manager HEMBREE delivered a staff report. On October 27, 2025,
  Councilmember Maza requested more information about the increase in nitrous oxide related
  arrests by the Alhambra Police Department (APD), the sale of nitrous oxide in the City and a
  draft Ordinance to regulate the sale of nitrous oxide. There was full support from the Council
  on this request. Nitrous oxide, commonly known as “laughing gas” or “whippets,” has become
  a growing public health and safety concern in Alhambra and throughout California. The APD,
  along with communities across the nation, have seen an increase in arrests and incidents
  related to the sale of nitrous oxide. To date, there were 5 authorized smoke shops in the City
  of Alhambra, of those, one was not open to the public and APD has found the 4 remaining sell
  nitrous oxide, presumably for recreational use. California Penal Code § 381b prohibits
  possession or use of nitrous oxide for intoxication, and the recreational sale of nitrous oxide is
  not harmless. Short-term effects include disorientation, nausea, blackouts, and impaired motor
  control-creating immediate risk to users and the public, particularly when combined with
  driving. Chronic misuse poses even more serious consequences including brain damage,
  irreversible nerve damage, paralysis, cognitive impairment, and even death. Due to the public
  safety risk, there has been an increase in Southern California jurisdictions adopting ordinances
  prohibiting the sale, distribution and recreational use of nitrous oxide, including the cities of;
  3
1-12-26
   Rialto, Bell, Huntington Beach, Santa Ana, Costa Mesa, Newport Beach, Fullerton and County
  of Orange.

  Discussion:  Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Lieutenant LEE discussed the
  five retailers selling nitrous oxide in the City. Councilmember WANG and Director of
  Community Development HO discussed if there were regulations governing hours of operation
  for smoke shops. Ms. WANG suggested that staff look at options and tools to better regulate
  businesses such as smoke shops or businesses which could raise community concerns and
  requested that staff explore options for these businesses to obtain a Conditional Use Permit
  through the Planning Commission. Councilmember MAZA thanked staff for their work on the
  ordinance and supported Ms. Wang’s suggestions. Councilmember LEE recalled Council’s
  approval of a past ordinance to prohibit the sale of flavored tobacco products.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its first reading the following
  ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M26-4856: An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of
  Alhambra, California, amending Title IX (Public Peace and Safety) of the
  Alhambra Municipal Code to include Chapter 9.19 (Prohibition on Sale or
  Distribution of Nitrous Oxide) and determining adoption of this Ordinance is
  exempt from CEQA

  which ordinance would return for a second reading and adoption the next regular
  City Council meeting.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

LEE:  Councilmember Lee recused herself from the discussion of Item No. 3 due to property
  which may be affected by the Ordinance. Ms. LEE left Council Chambers at 7:03 p.m.

5.  RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING NEW  FEES  FOR  HISTORIC  PRESERVATION
  APPLICATIONS – F2M20-51, R2M25-42

  Director of Community Development HO delivered a staff report. At the October 27, 2025
  regular City Council meeting, Historic Preservation application fees were discussed and
  continued. The Council directed staff to return with a 50% reduction of application fees for
  certain applications with an analysis of the impact to the General Fund. In addition, the Council
  directed staff to incorporate tiers to full cost recovery. Staff presented information regarding
  the proposed historic preservation application fees which establish new fees at 50% cost for
  certain historic preservation applications, include a 50% fee reduction for applications related
  to Designation, Certificate of Appropriateness and Mills Act, include no fee reductions for
  applications related to Certificate of Demolition, Economic Hardship or Appeals and the
  bundling of applications at reduced rate. Staff also discussed the phased approach to 100%
  cost recovery as well as General Fund impacts.

  Public Comment:
  1) Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St., supported some of the changes and suggested Council review
  4
1-12-26
   the progress after one year.

  2) Sawyer BROOKS, 118 E. McLean St., expressed concerns with the City’s subsidization of fees
  and suggested a cap on applications. He made further suggestions for application fees and
  policies.

  3) Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the study included with the staff report and
  echoed Ms. Ng’s suggestion for additional review and data collection. He supported some of
  the changes to the fee schedule.

  4) Melissa MICHELSON, via Zoom, supported some of the changes to the fee schedule and
  suggested further review of the progress of the program.

  Discussion: Councilmember WANG agreed with the suggestion to review the fee schedule
  after one year. She also stressed the importance of providing information to the public
  regarding the phasing in of the fee schedule. Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER suggested a
  review of the entire Historic Preservation program in one year’s time. Councilmember MAZA
  also spoke in favor of the reduced fees and agreed with Council to review the fee schedule
  after one year. Mr. MAZA and Mr. HO discussed the certificate of appropriateness process
  and the Mills Act agreement. Mayor MALONEY supported the proposed fees and went on to
  discuss comments made. He supported a review of the program.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M25-42 entitled: A Resolution
  of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, establishing new fees for Historic
  Preservation Applications to set fees for certain Historic Preservation applications at 50% of
  the full cost from FY 2025 up to FY 2027, 75% for FY 2027, and 100% for FY 2028 and onward
  subject to annual adjustment thereafter based on the Consumer Price Index (CPI) at July 1 of
  each fiscal year; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s
  action.

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  LEE

LEE:  Councilmember Lee returned to Council chambers at 7:03 p.m.

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 23): (TIME LIMITATIONS: 5 MINUTES PER SPEAKER FOR

6.  RESOLUTION APPROVING CHANGES TO THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA COMPENSATION
  PLAN AND SALARY SCHEDULE FOR PART-TIME JOB CLASSIFICATIONS – F2M26-2,
  R2M26-1

  California Public Employees’ Retirement Law requires the City Council to approve and adopt
  salary schedules and pay rates for job classifications at a public meeting. Effective January 1,
  2026, the State of California Department of Industrial Relations Minimum Wage Order
  mandates that minimum wage for employers with 26 or more employees be increased from
  $16.50 per hour to $16.90 per hour. The proposed Resolution provided for increases for part-

  5
1-12-26
   time hourly classifications to ensure compliance with the upcoming State of California
  mandated minimum wage increase. The salary schedule, attached to the Resolution was
  reflective of increases in order to bring part-time hourly classifications into compliance. To
  ensure compliance, the new part-time salary schedule would be effective on the pay period
  beginning January 1, 2026. Additionally, due to an anticipated retirement and upcoming
  staffing needs, a part-time Housing Assistant classification was added to the salary schedule.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., spoke in support of the salary
  increases for part-time job classifications and discussed the history of worker’s rights and state
  increases to minimum wage.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M26-1 entitled: A Resolution
  of the Alhambra City Council approving changes to the City of Alhambra Compensation Plan
  and Salary Schedule for part-time job classifications approving changes to the City of
  Alhambra Compensation Plan and Salary Schedule for part-time job classifications; and,
  directed the Finance Director to make the necessary budget adjustments to comply with the
  State mandated minimum wage increase. (M2M26-1)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  WANG, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

7.  APPROPRIATE OPIOID SETTLEMENT FUNDS FOR THE PURCHASE OF A DRUG
  INCINERATOR – F2M25-17, M2M26-2

  The City received a proportioned share of funding from opioid settlements, which funds were
  subject to guidelines under the administration of the California Department of Health Services.
  City staff recently identified the purchase of a drug incinerator as a possible use of opioid
  settlement funding. An incinerator is a portable drug terminator that properly disposes of
  narcotics, paraphernalia and bio-hazard materials. Currently, the Police Department disposes
  of confiscated narcotics through a third-party vendor. Purchasing the incinerator would allow
  the Police Department to properly dispose of narcotics onsite, as needed. Alhambra has
  received an approved funding application form the California Department of Health Services
  for the purchase of the incinerator at a cost of $6,700. An appropriation of funds was needed
  to finalize the proposed purchase.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council directed the Finance Director to appropriate $6,700 in
  expenditures for opioid settlement funds under the 2025-26 Fiscal Year Budget for the
  purchase of a drug incinerator for the Alhambra Police Department; and, directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action. (M2M26-2)

  Vote:  Moved:  ANDRADE-STADLER Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  WANG, LEE, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY
  Noes:  NONE

11.  CONTRACT AMENDMENT: WIRELESS MOBILE SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH T-
  MOBILE – F2M22-6B, C2M22-60, M2M26-5

  On November 14, 2022, the City Council approved an agreement with T-Mobile USA, Inc. for
  Connecting Heroes Program wireless mobile services through May 2023 for an amount
  estimated at $16,647 annually. Since the initial contract award, the City Council approved three
  subsequent contract amendments to add various services and to extend the term of the
  agreement. The Alhambra Police Department now requested to add an additional 26 Aircards
  which would allow officers to utilize their MDCs outside of the patrol vehicle for an annual cost
  of $10,483.20 as well as a router for the Drone as First Responder Program that would require
  an annual fee of $492. The pricing for T-Mobile was based off the NASPO ValuePoint Contract
  with the State of Utah for wireless data, voice and accessories which would be effective
  through August 11, 2029. Per Section 3.36.080(B)(3) of the Alhambra Municipal Code, the
  City as the option to purchase service through a cooperative agreement to obtain competitive
  pricing.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved an amendment, subject to final language

14.  APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT WITH LENCO INDUSTRIES, INC. FOR THE PURCHASE
  OF AN ARMORED VEHICLE – F2M26-6A, C2M26-2, M2M26-7

  Currently, the Alhambra Police Department responds to various incidents by utilizing standard
  issued patrol vehicles. When an incident requires a vehicle offering enhanced protection, such
  as the routine execution of search warrants or other high-risk operations, the Department must
  rely on borrowing an Armored Rescue Vehicle (ARV) from neighboring cities including San
  Gabriel, Monterey Park, Baldwin Park, Arcadia, and Glendale. The ARV could also be used in
  response to critical incidents to enhance community and officer safety and improve scene
  containment and stabilization. Lenco Industries, Inc. provided a quote of $123,690 for a used
  2006 Lenco G2 Bearcat, which was refurbished in 2017. Staff recommended the purchase of
  a used ARV because a new ARV takes approximately 12-18 months to manufacture and can
  cost $320,000. Lenco is the sole source as other companies do not have the availability to a
  used ARV. Sole source purchase is allowable per Alhambra Municipal Code Section
  3.36.080(B)(2).

  Public Comment:  Sawyer BROOKS, 118 E. McLean St., spoke in support of Alhambra
  Police Department but expressed concerns with the use of militarized equipment which reduce
  community trust and increase officer perceptions of threat in diverse urban communities. He
  urged Council to either decline the purchase or request staff return with a clearer report as to
  the potential uses of the vehicle. He also questioned the remaining life of an older vehicle and
  the remaining costs associated with it.

  Discussion: Councilmember WANG and Police Chief KENNEDY discussed the contract for
  the purchase of an armored vehicle and the potential uses of the vehicle such as rescue for
  officers or citizens during high-risk situations, serving search warrants and de-escalation of
  potentially high-risk situations. Vice Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER and Chief KENNEDY
  discussed school lockdowns and the potential use of armored vehicles. Councilmember LEE
  and Chief KENNEDY discussed the current practice of borrowing armored vehicles from other
  cities, the availability of used vehicles, and the availability of new vehicles. Ms. LEE discussed
  the appearance of the vehicle with Chief KENNEDY and City Manager BINNQUIST.
  Councilmember MAZA supported the purchase of the vehicle and discussed the costs of
  armored vehicles. Mayor MALONEY spoke regarding the uses of armored vehicles for limited
  situations and supported the purchase. He went on to speak in support of the Alhambra Police
  Department practices to deescalate situations.

  Action Taken:  City Council awarded a contract, subject to final language approval by
  the City Manager and City Attorney, to Lenco Industries, Inc. for the purchase of an Armored
  Rescue Vehicle in an amount not to exceed $123,690; authorized the Chief of Police to

18.  A RESOLUTION FOR THE APPLICATION AND CERTIFICATION AGREEMENT FOR THE
  CERTIFIED LOCAL GOVERNMENT (CLG) PRESERVATION PROGRAM – F2M26-21,
  R2M26-2

  The Certified Local Government (CLG) program is a partnership between local governments,
  the State Office of Historic Preservation (OHP), and the National Park Service (NPS). Program
  benefits include access to technical assistance and potential grant funding opportunities to
  support the City’s preservation efforts. The Historic Preservation Commission and City Council
  expressed an interest in the City of Alhambra becoming a Certified Local Government. With
  the adoption of the Historic Preservation Program last year, the City would now be eligible to
  apply for CLG status. As part of the application process, a City Council resolution was required
  to approve the application before submitting it to the State. The Resolution also authorized the
  City Manager and the Director of Community Development, as an Authorized Deputy, to sign
  the Certification Agreement for the CLG Program and coordinate, process, and execute all
  contracts, agreements, amendments, and ancillary documents within the scope of the
  application for certification.

  Resolution and further discussed the Certified Local Government Preservation Program.

  Discussion: Councilmember LEE and Director of Community Development HO discussed

  Action Taken:  City Council adopted Resolution No. R2M26-2 entitled: a Resolution
  of the City of Alhambra City Council approving the Application and Certification Agreement for
  the Certified Local Government Historic Preservation Program approving the application and
  authorizing the City Manager to sign the Certification Agreement for the Certified Local
  Government (CLG) Program.

  OF AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE BY MODIFYING

  AMENDMENTS, ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS THERETO – F2M25-60, O2M26-4854,
  O2M26-4855, N2M26-1

  Every three years, the State of California updates the California Code of Regulations, Title 24.
  The 2025 California Fire Code and the 2025 Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) Code became
  effective statewide on January 1, 2026. Local jurisdictions are required to adopt these codes
  and may amend them where necessary due to local climatic, geological, or topographic
  conditions. The Fire Department reviewed the 2025 California Fire Code and recommends the
  adoption of the code along with the previously approved amendments outlined in the January
  12, 2026 staff report by the Fire Chief and Deputy Fire Marshall. Only the section numbers
  were updated to align with the new code arrangement. California Codes can be viewed at
  https://www.dqs.ca.qov/BSC/Codes. The findings required by the Health and Safety Code
  §18941.5 accompany the proposed ordinances as Exhibit A. These updates are necessary to
  maintain consistent and enforceable fire-safety standards within the City.

  Discussion:  None.
